preregistered_rule.scientific_question: Does nested observer-boundary cancellation survive materially different Mooney-Rivlin baseline partitions at fixed total small-strain shear modulus?
preregistered_rule.samples: 25 equal-area pressure points from x=0.05 to x=0.80
preregistered_rule.material_change_only: baseline Wi = 0.5(1-f)(I1bar-3)+0.5 f(I2bar-3); coefficient sum remains 0.5, so total small-strain shear modulus is fixed
preregistered_rule.level1: for EACH new f: direct-vs-state added-band angle >160 deg; direct/state off-interface norm ratio in [0.75,1.33]; total added-band off-interface norm <=0.35*max(direct,state)
preregistered_rule.level2: for EACH new f: total added-band off-interface component angle >150 deg to pre-existing interior off-interface component; adding it reduces inner off-interface norm by >=50%
preregistered_rule.validity: all centered finite-difference step-angle checks <0.01 deg; decomposition closure relative error <1e-5; re-equilibrated preload/twist residual infinity norms <1e-7
preregistered_rule.verdict_rule: both new material baselines pass both levels -> MATERIAL_BASELINE_NESTED_CANCELLATION_REPLICATED
preregistered_rule.claim_boundary: A pass establishes robustness only over f=0.15, 0.289340, 0.45 in this incompressible Mooney-Rivlin baseline family, not arbitrary hyperelastic energies.
